qualifying_findings.title: token-optimizer-mcp command injection advisory
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: GitHub Advisory Database published GHSA-86qw-c7qw-gp4c for token-optimizer-mcp, identifying a high-severity command-injection issue, CVE-2026-55157, in MCP tooling that runs optimizer-related commands.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: token-optimizer-mcp, affected versions as recorded by the GitHub advisory; exact downstream deployments depend on package use.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP servers extend agent tool authority. Command injection in an MCP server can turn delegated tool use into host command execution, requiring package version control, sandboxing, and least-privilege runtime isolation.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad MCP server and package catalog context belongs upstream; this repository should keep the security-specific command-injection implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on in-window status and advisory relevance from GitHub's visible publication date; affected-range details should be rechecked during ingest.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check whether a local durable page should be created for MCP package command execution boundaries or folded into an existing MCP server vulnerability page.
Verify patched version and mitigation language from package metadata or maintainer release notes before writing durable guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: swagger-testcase-mcp code injection CVE
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-19765 was published for swagger-testcase-mcp, describing code injection through a crafted swagger file in the Python MCP server package.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: swagger-testcase-mcp Python package before the fixed release identified by downstream vulnerability databases.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Swagger or OpenAPI documents are likely to be treated as data inputs for API-aware agents, but this issue turns untrusted API description input into executable code risk inside an MCP server.

upstream_routing.reason: General MCP package catalog ownership is upstream; keep local detail to untrusted API-spec input and MCP execution risk.
General API-test generation workflow implications belong upstream to AI-assisted development practice; keep only the security boundary here.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence: multiple vulnerability databases reference the CVE and package; the CVE page was not fully rendered in the fetched view, so ingest should verify authoritative record fields.
follow_up_actions: Fetch CVE JSON or advisory metadata during ingest to confirm affected versions and remediation.
Compare with existing MCP vulnerability leaves before creating a new page.

qualifying_findings.title: Australian Cyber Security Centre updated AI agent action guidance
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: ACSC visibly updated guidance on 2026-08-14 about AI agents taking unexpected actions, emphasizing that agent authority, tool access, and autonomous execution can create cyber-security risk when actions exceed user intent or organizational controls.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Organizations deploying AI agents with tool access, delegated action, browser or workflow automation, and access to enterprise data or systems.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The update directly addresses delegated authority, approval boundaries, monitoring, and operational controls for agentic systems, which are core local wiki ownership areas.

upstream_routing.reason: General agent workflow governance belongs upstream; local coverage should focus on cyber-security controls and delegated-authority risk.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on official source and visible updated date; ingest should capture the exact controls from the source page without over-quoting.
follow_up_actions: Map ACSC controls to existing local pages on approval boundaries, delegated authority, and agent action runtime hooks.
Check whether an official companion PDF or archived version exists for durable citation.

qualifying_findings.title: Tenable agentic AI threat-cluster report

visible_dates.source: Tenable blog search result and page metadata

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Tenable published a report grouping seven agentic-AI security incidents across three actor categories, framing recurring risks around autonomous agents, delegated system access, prompt or tool misuse, and enterprise exposure.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Enterprise agentic-AI deployments and integrations with tool access, data access, cloud resources, or developer environments.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The cluster analysis is a public security synthesis of recurring agentic-AI incident patterns and can support local threat modeling, assurance gates, and incident taxonomy updates.

upstream_routing.reason: Broad vendor and agentic-AI ecosystem context belongs upstream; local coverage should preserve incident patterns and security lessons.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence: search and page metadata identify an in-window Tenable report; ingest should refetch the article and verify individual incident claims before durable synthesis.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, split specific named incidents into existing incident or threat leaves where they add new facts.
Avoid treating Tenable's clustering taxonomy as authoritative without preserving attribution.

qualifying_findings.title: U.S. grant notice for AI supply-chain security provenance platform
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: A U.S. government Grants.gov opportunity for Pax Silica describes an AI supply-chain security credentialing and provenance platform, tying provenance, verification, and supply-chain trust to AI system security.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI supply-chain credentialing, provenance, and verification controls; grant opportunity rather than deployed product advisory.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The notice is a public official signal that AI supply-chain provenance and credentialing are being funded as security infrastructure, relevant to model, artifact, dependency, and deployment trust boundaries.

upstream_routing.reason: Company and platform background belongs upstream if Pax Silica becomes durable; local coverage should keep the security-provenance implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence: official source and in-window date qualify, but because it is a funding notice rather than an incident or advisory, ingest should decide whether it merits durable coverage or only a routing note.
follow_up_actions: Check whether the opportunity exposes agency, award, or abstract details suitable for an AI supply-chain controls page.
Exclude from durable security pages if the notice proves to be only a generic funding listing without concrete control detail.
